purpose: Cost-effective current systems and secondary-market accelerators with unusually useful memory capacity for local LLM inference.
notes: Retail and marketplace prices are point-in-time observations; shipping, tax, import fees and configuration differences can materially change delivered cost.
Secondary-market accelerators may require server airflow, custom cooling/ducting, legacy software stacks or unusual power cabling.
Price-per-memory-GB is a capacity metric only; it is not a substitute for tokens/sec, software maturity, power efficiency or total-system cost.

hardware.product: Framework Desktop DIY Edition - Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / 128GB
hardware.model_size_practicality: 128GB unified memory is suitable for large quantized models; Framework publishes a 38 tok/s gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 result on this configuration. Exact context length and KV-cache requirements still reduce usable model capacity.
hardware.clusterability: 5GbE plus USB4; Framework explicitly documents multi-node llama.cpp RPC use and Mini-ITX density of two mainboards per 2U chassis.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: medium-high for the memory capacity; 120W sustained processor power is far below multi-GPU servers, but whole-system wall power should be measured before energy budgeting.
hardware.performance_per_watt_status: vendor LLM throughput exists, but comparable wall-power benchmark is not published on the cited configuration

pricing.note: 128GB Ryzen AI Max+ 395 mainboard display price observed on the localized Framework storefront; mainboard includes the pre-installed heatsink/fan mount but requires storage and other system parts.
Refurbished 128GB Desktop DIY Edition observed below the standalone 128GB mainboard price; storage, AC cable, fan, tiles, expansion cards and OS are not included.

software: llama.cpp CUDA builds when compiled for Pascal
hardware.software_lifecycle_warning: CUDA Toolkit 13.x removed offline compilation and library support for Pascal. CUDA 12.x remains the practical build ceiling for native Pascal targets, so long-term software compatibility is a material risk.
hardware.model_size_practicality: 24GB VRAM is useful for roughly 20B-30B class quantized models depending on quantization, context and runtime overhead; larger models generally require CPU offload or multiple GPUs.
quantization_compatibility: GGUF/llama.cpp CUDA subject to Pascal-compatible builds
modern low-bit tensor-core paths unavailable because Pascal predates Tensor Cores
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low-medium; memory-per-dollar is attractive but 250W board power and required forced airflow make it less suitable than modern SFF or unified-memory systems for constrained solar budgets.

pricing.note: Representative used P40 24GB listing price visible in eBay Canada search results; shipping, taxes and seller condition vary.

interconnect: 92 GB/s peak aggregate link bandwidth vendor specification
hardware.cooling: passive; server-class forced airflow required unless safely adapted by the system builder
hardware.software_lifecycle_warning: MI50/gfx906 appears in current ROCm architecture references, but older ROCm support matrices have marked MI50 deprecated/limited. Verify the exact ROCm release and framework before purchase.
hardware.model_size_practicality: 32GB HBM2 provides enough capacity for many 30B-class quantized models and the 1 TB/s bandwidth is excellent for decode, but unsupported runtime combinations can erase the hardware advantage.
quantization_compatibility: runtime-specific lower-bit support must be verified
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low; exceptional bandwidth-per-dollar is offset by 300W board power, passive cooling requirements and older software support.

pricing.note: Calgary-based used MI50 32GB listing showed CA$600 with more than 10 available; marketplace condition and availability can change quickly.
